visualReview.notes: Inspected eight portable frames of the pediment, recessed main arch, trefoil shrine, north belfry, buttresses and adjoining tiled ranges.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected eight dated viewer views. The coral masonry, wooden upper convent, clay roof tiles and painted sheet-metal nave roof remain distinguishable. The main belfry opening renders as a true opening.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 24 context, detail and transition views. The stepped roof pitch, long lower ranges, stone supports, main arch and open belfry persist at every distance.

geographicReview.notes: The entrance faces the east forecourt and the attached ranges retain the original mapped envelope. The separate belfry is placed north of the façade as documented, with approximate dimensions and registration. Original terrain meets the plinth and steps.

fidelityReview.scope: The main Boljoon Church and its attached convent, with an approximate north belfry, in the November 2021 documented configuration. Includes the pedimented east front, buttressed coral-stone nave, metal nave roof and tiled convent. The detached El Gran Baluarte, school, cemetery and interiors are separate.
fidelityReview.notes: The museum’s written evidence constrains the two nave roof slopes and materials, east composition, timber convent and north belfry position. The belfry envelope, ornament, height, historic paint and minor openings are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: No source imagery was used. The Qualla public-domain candidates depict museum exhibits, and the published direct architectural photographs carry attribution licenses. Used the official museum’s written facts and mapped dimensions.

primaryFactsReview.notes: The named sixteen-corner church outline and the museum’s written architectural facts support the church, attached convent and approximate north belfry. The main roof pitches match the reported angles. Sections, tower footprint, ornament and finish are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: November 2021 main Boljoon Church, attached convent, and approximate north belfry

limitations: The complete mapped church and adjoining convent follow the original sixteen-corner outline. Internal massing divisions, eaves, ornament, openings and the palette are estimates from written facts and the mapped exterior.
The north belfry location follows the museum description. Its footprint, heights and roofing profile are estimates. The separately named El Gran Baluarte and other outbuildings are outside scope.
The National Museum reports upper and lower main-roof slopes of 39 and 28 degrees and the 2007 galvanized iron covering. The position of the slope break is estimated.
The field preserves the original provider samples. The entrance and foundation are registered to approximate local grade.
